Docs.param: The items to embed, in order: 1 to 32 items. Currently a request can have at most one `text` or `query` item and at most 8 images. Images can be up to 20 MiB and 50 megapixels each (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP), with at most 20 MiB of images per request. The request body can be up to 30,000,000 bytes.
The model to use, for example `microsoft-embedding-1-large` (Microsoft Embedding 1-large).
The kind of vectors to return. Defaults to `dense`.
The number of dimensions per vector; with `dense_multi`, of the dense vector. Must be a value the model supports for the requested vector kind; the model's native width is the default.
For `dense_multi` only: the number of dimensions per multi-vector. Must be a value the model supports for multi-vectors; the model's native multi-vector width is the default.
For `multi` and `dense_multi` only: the most multi-vectors to return per item.
The numeric type of the returned values, for every vector in the response. Defaults to `float32` for `dense` and `float16` for `multi` and `dense_multi`.
How vectors are encoded in the response. Defaults to `float`.
How to return the results. An explicit value wins. Without it, a request with images gets `link` where the endpoint has a result store, and every other request gets `inline`.
The cancellation token that can be used to cancel the operation.
Docs.summary: Embeds text, queries and document images and returns dense or multi-vector embeddings as numbers or base64. Text and queries are sent inline. Images are read from the caller's Azure Blob Storage with a caller-signed user delegation SAS (Microsoft Entra callers only). Results come back in the response or, with `delivery: link`, as a time-limited read-only link.
